orgs.name: Alcoholics Anonymous — District 10, Kitsap Peninsula
services: Official A.A. District 10 (Kitsap Peninsula, Western Washington Area 72) resource site: current A.A. meeting guide for Kitsap and North Mason counties (printable PDF) and links to the official Meeting Guide app
Kitsap-area A.A. is also served by the Puget Sound Central Service Office 24-hour hotline, 253-474-8897 (Tacoma)
orgs.serves: People in Kitsap County seeking A.A. meetings

orgs.name: Bremerton Foodline
services: Grocery-store-style free food shopping (fresh produce, dairy, proteins, canned and pantry goods, hygiene and personal care items) at 1600 12th St, Bremerton — walk-in, no income proof or appointment needed, Sun–Wed 11 AM–6 PM, once per week
orgs.serves: Bremerton-area residents in need of food

orgs.name: Bremerton Housing Authority
services: Public housing and affordable developments in Bremerton (Wright Court, Charter House, Tara Heights, Winfield, Shadow Creek, Tamarack, The Firs, Casa Del Sol, Bay Vista South/West, The Summit, Bay Vista Commons assisted living)
Administers the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program throughout Kitsap and Mason counties
Evergreen Bright Start: 24 units of housing for youth ages 18–24 (2024 CAPER: $3,424,697 county CIAH); HOME-ARP homeless prevention and housing navigator program (772 households assisted in 2024)
orgs.serves: Low-income households in Bremerton and (for vouchers) Kitsap and Mason counties

orgs.name: Catholic Community Services of Western Washington — Housing & Essential Needs (HEN), Kitsap County
services: Kitsap County Housing and Essential Needs (HEN) program, operated by CCS (office 360-373-0638, Mon–Fri 8 AM–4 PM): rental assistance, security deposits and move-in costs, bus vouchers, monthly essential-needs items (hygiene and household basics) and case management for DSHS-referred clients (ABD/incapacitated)
BRIDGE program: transitional support for clients moving to SSI/SSDI (pay 30% of income, up to one year)

Benedict House, 250 S Cambrian Ave, Bremerton: emergency shelter for homeless men (24 beds plus 3 medical respite beds) with meals and case management — the only facility for homeless men in Kitsap County; apply via the Housing Solutions Center, 360-473-2035
orgs.serves: Kitsap County: HEN serves DSHS-referred adults; Benedict House serves homeless men

orgs.name: Central Kitsap Food Bank
services: Grocery-style food bank at 3537 Anderson Hill Rd, Silverdale: clients shop the aisles with a volunteer for fresh produce, refrigerated and frozen goods and shelf-stable staples; curbside pickup by phone reservation
Programs for seniors and children and community resource information at no cost
orgs.serves: Central Kitsap residents in need of food

orgs.name: Eagles Wings Coordinated Care
services: Certified recovery housing across Kitsap County (WAQRR Level 2 accredited residences in Bremerton, Port Orchard and Silverdale; transitional housing with wrap-around services — the org's own profile reports 100+ beds in 13 houses); housing application on the org's site; admin office 3029 Wheaton Way, Bremerton
Medical Respite Program: referrals accepted for people experiencing homelessness who are recovering from acute illness or injury
Rental assistance funded by Kitsap County CIAH (2024 CAPER: $245,556 to 158 households — rent arrears, utilities and move-in costs); supports Kitsap County therapeutic court programs
orgs.serves: People in recovery from chemical dependency and people experiencing homelessness in Kitsap County

orgs.name: Helpline House
services: Food bank at 282 Knechtel Way NE, Bainbridge Island (Mon–Fri 10 AM–4 PM), open to any Washington State resident
Social services (Mon–Fri 9 AM–5 PM): housing and utility support, counseling, and resource navigation for Bainbridge Island neighbors
orgs.serves: Bainbridge Island residents; food bank open to any Washington State resident

orgs.name: Housing Kitsap (Kitsap County Consolidated Housing Authority)
services: Affordable rental communities across Kitsap County (Finch Place, Fjord Manor, Golden Tides II/III, Madrona Manor, Port Orchard Vista, Windsong and others — senior, disabled, USDA Rural Development and tax-credit homes, some with subsidized rents); waitlist applications online or on paper; main office 2244 NW Bucklin Hill Rd, Silverdale
Rental assistance funded by Kitsap County CIAH (2024 CAPER: $116,039 to 29 households) and home rehabilitation (2024 CAPER: $110,501 CDBG, 11 homes)
Mutual Self-Help Housing: groups of families build their own homes (Kitsap and Mason counties)
orgs.serves: Income-eligible households across Kitsap County

orgs.name: Housing Resources Bainbridge
services: Affordable rental housing on Bainbridge Island: 73 rental units downtown (affordable units with rent set by government funders for households up to 80% AMI; subsidized units with project-based vouchers for households under 50% AMI — subsidized waitlist closed at fetch time); all vacancies filled from waitlists
Community land trust: permanently affordable homes for purchase by income-eligible buyers (80% AMI, a few up to 120%)

Independent Living program: free health-and-safety home modifications (grab bars, accessibility, weatherization) for Bainbridge Island households at or below 80% AMI; Western View Terrace rehabilitation funded by county CDBG (2024 CAPER: $235,347, 8 units)
orgs.serves: Income-eligible households seeking housing on Bainbridge Island

orgs.name: Kitsap Community Resources
services: Housing Solutions Center (HSC) — Kitsap County's Coordinated Entry first step, staffed by KCR and funded by the Kitsap County Housing & Homelessness Division: connects people to emergency shelter, rental and deposit assistance, and landlord referrals. Sites: 1201 Park Ave, Bremerton; 3200 SE Rainshadow Ct, Port Orchard; 787 Liberty Lane NW, Poulsbo; and at Helpline House, Bainbridge Island
Energy Assistance (LIHEAP / PSE / CARES, Oct 1–Aug 15) for income-eligible Kitsap residents, plus weatherization referrals — 845 8th St, Bremerton; energy line 360-479-1507
orgs.serves: Kitsap County residents who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or need help with energy costs

orgs.name: Kitsap Immigrant Assistance Center
services: Immigration Legal Services: DOJ-accredited representatives and volunteer lawyers handle asylum, green cards and renewals, naturalization, visas, DACA filings/renewals and work authorizations (600+ immigrants per year)
Family Services: connecting immigrants with rent assistance, clothing, baby items and pantry staples; scheduling for free medical and dental clinic appointments; translation help with medical bills
Tax & Business Services: state and federal tax filing and business-license applications for immigrants
orgs.serves: Immigrants and their families in Kitsap County

orgs.name: Kitsap Legal Aid Services
services: Free civil legal aid for low-income Kitsap County residents (under 200% of the federal poverty level) through volunteer attorneys: family law, domestic-violence fallout, housing matters including eviction defense for tenants facing eviction, wills and estates, bankruptcy and other civil issues
Office: 500 Pacific Ave, Suite 401, Bremerton; intake Tue/Thu 10 AM–4 PM
orgs.serves: Low-income residents of Kitsap County (civil matters only, no criminal cases)

orgs.name: Kitsap Mental Health Services
services: Comprehensive behavioral health care for children, adults and families across Kitsap County (6,000+ clients per year; Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic since 2023) — outpatient, crisis, and residential services from campuses in Bremerton, Port Orchard and Poulsbo
orgs.serves: Kitsap County residents needing mental-health or substance-use services; Medicaid-primary but no one is turned away

orgs.name: Kitsap Rescue Mission
services: Pacific Building Housing Navigation Center, 4459 SE Mile Hill Dr, Port Orchard: 75-bed, 24/7 continuous-stay low-barrier emergency shelter for individuals and families (pets welcome), with on-site behavioral health, housing navigation and supportive services; access via the Housing Solutions Center (Coordinated Entry)
Meals, showers and laundry for shelter guests (guest accounts on the org's own site; 2025 org-reported outcomes: 23,646 meals, 22,074 bed nights, 72 transitions to permanent housing)
Shelter and supportive services under Kitsap County MHCDTC contract KC-027-26 ($268,224, Jan–Dec 2026), focused on behavioral health, substance-use treatment linkage and stabilization
orgs.serves: People experiencing homelessness in Kitsap County, including families and people with pets

orgs.name: North Kitsap Fishline
services: Free grocery-style Food Market at 19705 Viking Ave NW, Poulsbo (register on the 2nd floor; shop once weekly; fresh produce, meat, dairy, canned goods, baby food and diapers)
Fishline On the Move mobile food market with Navigator support; Navigators available by appointment for resource navigation
orgs.serves: North Kitsap residents (Poulsbo, Keyport, Suquamish area)

orgs.name: Olalla Recovery Centers
services: Olalla Guest Lodge, 12850 Lala Cove Ln SE, Olalla: residential (inpatient) alcohol and drug treatment with holistic therapies including acupuncture for detoxification, yoga/meditation and nutrition education
Outpatient treatment program in Gig Harbor; specialized women's programs and a Family Education Program; Native American Recovery Path
orgs.serves: Adults seeking substance-use treatment on the Kitsap Peninsula

orgs.name: Peninsula Community Health Services
services: Federally Qualified Health Center founded in Bremerton (1987): primary medical, dental, behavioral health counseling, substance use treatment, pharmacy services and health education; all patients accepted regardless of insurance or ability to pay (sliding fee scale)
Medical respite facility (22 rooms) in development with Kitsap County CIAH capital support; partner in the Pacific Building shelter's on-site care
orgs.serves: Kitsap Peninsula residents, regardless of insurance or ability to pay

orgs.name: Scarlet Road
services: Holistic aftercare for people who have been sexually exploited: survivor-led outreach, intensive case management, mentoring and skill building (drop-in/office 1222 Park Ave, Bremerton)

Flexible rental assistance with intensive case management for adult victims of sex trafficking and sexual exploitation, under Kitsap County MHCDTC contract KC-033-26 ($120,540, Jan–Dec 2026, est. 30 people/year)
orgs.serves: Adults in Kitsap County who have experienced sexual exploitation or trafficking

orgs.name: ShareNet Food Bank
services: Emergency food bank at 25994 Barber Cut Off Rd NE, Kingston (Tue & Fri 10 AM–2 PM, curbside pickup, no pre-application)
Screened emergency power (utility) assistance and rental assistance for clients facing service-interruption notices or eviction
Food2GO weekend backpack food program for schoolchildren at all Kingston public schools; thrift store with clothing vouchers for food bank clients
orgs.serves: Greater Kingston area (Kingston, Hansville, Port Gamble, Indianola, Eglon, Little Boston, and border addresses in Suquamish and Poulsbo)

orgs.name: South Kitsap Helpline
services: Food bank at 4215 SE Mile Hill Dr, Port Orchard (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 11 AM–5 PM): weekly shopping for dairy, meat, produce, canned goods, bread and frozen items; need-based, no appointment; non-food items on request (diapers, pet food, hygiene and laundry supplies)
TEFAP commodities three times per month; SNAP/WIC information and SNAP application help; Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program ($80 card) applications
orgs.serves: South Kitsap residents in need of food

orgs.name: St. Vincent de Paul Conference of Our Lady Star of the Sea (SVdP Bremerton)
services: Stella Maris House emergency shelter for women and women with children (referral via KCR Housing Solutions Center, 360-473-2035); Star of Hope campaign is expanding shelter beds from 30 to 47 and adding 38 transitional/permanent supportive units

Neighborhood Market & Resource Center: self-shopping, farmers-market-style food bank at 1117 N Callow Ave, Bremerton (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 10:30 AM–2:30 PM, no ID or proof of address required); Assistance Office on site (ext. 7)
